47501-married-love-a-new-contribution-to.creator: Unknown
47501-married-love-a-new-contribution-to.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Marie Stopes deals with subjects which are generally regarded as too sacred for an entirely frank treatment. Some earnest and delicate minds may feel apprehensive that such frankness in details is "dangerous," because the effect on prurient minds might be to give them food for their morbid fancies.

arxiv-2406-05231.title: The ULS23 Challenge: a Baseline Model and Benchmark Dataset for 3D Universal Lesion Segmentation in Computed Tomography Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2406-05231.creator: M.J.J. de Grauw, E.Th. Scholten, E.J. Smit, M.J.C.M. Rutten, M. Prokop, B. van Ginneken, A. Hering
arxiv-2406-05231.description: Abstract Size measurements of tumor manifestations on follow-up CT examinations are crucial for evaluating treatment outcomes in cancer patients. Efficient lesion segmentation can speed up these radiological workflows. While numerous benchmarks and challenges address lesion segmentation in specific organs like the liver, kidneys, and lungs, the larger variety of lesion types encountered in clinical practice demands a more universal approach.

arxiv-2407-12797.title: CEBench: A Benchmarking Toolkit for the Cost-Effectiveness of LLM Pipelines
arxiv-2407-12797.creator: Wenbo Sun, Jiaqi Wang, Qiming Guo, Ziyu Li, Wenlu Wang, Rihan Hai
arxiv-2407-12797.description: Abstract Online Large Language Model (LLM) services such as ChatGPT and Claude 3 have transformed business operations and academic research by effortlessly enabling new opportunities. However, due to data-sharing restrictions, sectors such as healthcare and finance prefer to deploy local LLM applications using costly hardware resources.

arxiv-2501-13058.title: A polynomial formula for the perspective four points problem
arxiv-2501-13058.creator: David Lehavi, Brian Osserman
arxiv-2501-13058.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by David Lehavi, Brian Osserman. We present a fast and accurate solution to the perspective n n -points problem, by way of a new approach to the n = 4 n=4 case. Our solution hinges on a novel separation of variables: given four 3D points and four corresponding 2D points on the camera canvas, we start by finding another set of 3D points, sitting on the rays connecting the camera to the 2D canvas points, so that the six pair-wise distances between these 3D points

arxiv-2502-13264.title: Violation of Pauli Limit at KTaO 3 (110) Interfaces
arxiv-2502-13264.creator: Samuel J. Poage, Xueshi Gao, Merve Baksi, Salva Salmani-Rezaie, David A. Muller, Divine P. Kumah, Chun Ning Lau, José Lorenzana, Maria N. Gastiasoro, Kaveh Ahadi
arxiv-2502-13264.description: Abstract Abstract The superconducting order parameter at the KTaO 3 interfaces and its dependence on interface orientation remains a subject of debate. The superconductivity at these interfaces exhibits strong resilience against in-plane magnetic field and violates Pauli limit. The interface orientation dependence of critical field and violation of Pauli limit, however, have not been investigated.

arxiv-2506-11275.title: Population-resolved measurement of an avoided crossing of light-dressed states
arxiv-2506-11275.creator: Noah Schlossberger, Nikunjkumar Prajapati, Eric B. Norrgard, Stephen P. Eckel, Christopher L. Holloway
arxiv-2506-11275.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Noah Schlossberger, Nikunjkumar Prajapati, Eric B. Norrgard, Stephen P. Eckel, Christopher L. Holloway. A two-level system coupled by a coherent field is a ubiquitous system in atomic and molecular physics. In the rotating wave approximation, the light-dressed states are well described by a simple 2 × \times 2 Hamiltonian which can be easily solved analytically and is thus used in quantum mechanics education and as a basis for intuition for more complicated systems.

arxiv-2508-05557.title: MV‑Debate: Multi-view Agent Debate with Dynamic Reflection Gating for Multimodal Harmful Content Detection in Social Media Thanks: Corresponding authors: yuntaodu@sdu.edu.cn, yijunt@amazon.com.
arxiv-2508-05557.description: Abstract Social media has evolved into a complex multimodal environment where text, images, and other signals interact to shape nuanced meanings, often concealing harmful intent. Identifying such intent, whether sarcasm, hate speech, or misinformation, remains challenging due to cross-modal contradictions, rapid cultural shifts, and subtle pragmatic cues.

arxiv-2510-15601.title: Kernel-Based Evaluation of Conditional Biological Sequence Models
arxiv-2510-15601.creator: Pierre Glaser, Steffanie Paul, Alissa M. Hummer, Charlotte M. Deane, Debora S. Marks, Alan N. Amin
arxiv-2510-15601.description: Abstract We propose a set of kernel-based tools to evaluate the designs and tune the hyperparameters of conditional sequence models, with a focus on problems in computational biology. The backbone of our tools is a new measure of discrepancy between the true conditional distribution and the model’s estimate, called the Augmented Conditional Maximum Mean Discrepancy (ACMMD).

arxiv-2510-18567.title: Contextual Search in Principal-Agent Games: The Curse of Degeneracy
arxiv-2510-18567.creator: Yiding Feng, Mengfan Ma, Bo Peng, Zongqi Wan
arxiv-2510-18567.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce and study contextual search in general principal-agent games, where a principal repeatedly interacts with agents by offering contracts based on contextual information and historical feedback, without knowing the agents’ true costs or rewards. Our model generalizes classical contextual pricing by accommodating richer agent action spaces.

arxiv-2510-24696.title: How Flat is a Plateau? Evolution of Late-Time TDE Disks
arxiv-2510-24696.creator: Yael Alush, Nicholas C. Stone, Sjoert van Velzen
arxiv-2510-24696.description: Abstract Late-time light curve plateaus in tidal disruption events (TDEs) are often approximated as flat and time-independent. This simplification is motivated by theoretical modeling of spreading late time TDE disks, which often predicts slow light curve evolution. However, if time evolution can be detected, late-time light curves will yield more information than has been previously accessible.

arxiv-2510-25004.title: Micro-Doppler signatures and object characterisation of space debris with radio telescopes
arxiv-2510-25004.description: Abstract This study presents a novel multi-static radar technique for space debris characterisation using micro-Doppler signatures, developed within the Southern Hemisphere Asteroid Radar Programme (SHARP). The method employs C-band continuous waveforms transmitted from NASA’s Deep Space Network (DSN) Canberra station, with reflected signals captured by distributed ground-based telescopes converted from astronomical to radar operations.

joh-andreae-stisseri-de-variis-erroribus.creator: Stisser, Johann Andreas, 1657-1700

pmc-10591587.title: P081 Experiences of men who have had bariatric surgery in New Zealand
pmc-10591587.creator: E Besley
pmc-10591587.description: IntroductionBariatric or weight loss surgery is currently the most effective method of long-term weight loss, and as obesity is a major risk factor for obstructive sleep apnoea, a potential treatment option. Approximately 80% of people who have bariatric surgery are women, however there is limited research regarding men, and none from New Zealand.

pmc-10628872.title: Tofacitinib as a Promising Therapeutic Option in Refractory Autoimmune-Mediated Vascular and Sclera Inflammation
pmc-10628872.creator: Theodoros Dimitroulas
pmc-10628872.description: athway constitutes a pivotal regulator of pro-inflammatory signal transduction, JAK inhibitors are considered to ameliorate the effects of several cytokines and provide a broader level of control in systemic auto-immune diseases beyond inflammatory arthritides.1 The latter is reflected in the growing number of studies exploring the efficacy of JAK inhibitors in new indications such as systemic lupus erythematosus or dermatomyositis.

pmc-11473400.title: Loss of DOCK2 potentiates Inflammatory Bowel Disease–associated colorectal cancer via immune dysfunction and IFNγ induction of IDO1 expression
pmc-11473400.creator: Antonia M D Churchhouse, Caroline V Billard, Toshiyasu Suzuki, Sebastian Ö G Pohl, Nora J Doleschall, Kevin Donnelly, Colin Nixon, Mark J Arends, Shahida Din, Kathryn Kirkwood, Jair Marques Junior, Alex Von Kriegsheim, Seth B Coffelt, Kevin B Myant
pmc-11473400.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Inflammatory Bowel Disease-associated colorectal cancer (IBD-CRC) is a known and serious complication of Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) affecting the colon. However, relatively little is known about the pathogenesis of IBD-associated colorectal cancer in comparison with its sporadic cancer counterpart. Here, we investigated the function of Dock2, a gene mutated in ~10% of IBD-associated colorectal cancers that encodes a guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF).

pmc-11487968.title: From virus to cancer: Epstein–Barr virus miRNA connection in Burkitt's lymphoma
pmc-11487968.creator: Shahram Jalilian, Mohammad-Navid Bastani
pmc-11487968.description: In Burkitt's lymphoma (BL), Epstein–Barr virus-encoded microRNAs (EBV miRNAs) are emerging as crucial regulatory agents that impact cellular and viral gene regulation. This review investigates the multifaceted functions of EBV miRNAs in the pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma. EBV miRNAs regulate several cellular processes that are essential for BL development, such as apoptosis, immune evasion, and cellular proliferation.

pmc-11509653.title: Peri-Implantitis-Associated Microbiota before and after Peri-Implantitis Treatment, the Biofilm “Competitive Balancing” Effect: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmc-11509653.creator: Federica Di Spirito, Massimo Pisano, Maria Pia Di Palo, Gianluigi Franci, Antonio Rupe, Antonino Fiorino, Carlo Rengo, Hidenobu Senpuku
pmc-11509653.description: This systematic review of RCTs aimed to characterize short- and long-term changes in peri-implantitis-associated microbiota (total biofilm microbial load and predominant pathogens’ counts) following (any) peri-implantitis treatment in systemically healthy, non-smoking, partially/totally edentulous adults. The study protocol, compliant with the PRISMA statement, was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024514521) before the literature search.

pmc-12052437.title: Presence of Echinococcus eggs in the environment and food: a review of current data and future prospects
pmc-12052437.creator: Roxanne Barosi, Gérald Umhang
pmc-12052437.description: he Northern Hemisphere (Deplazes et al., 2017; Massolo et al., 2022, Fig. 1). The highest AE disease burden is in Asia, especially China, while that for CE is more widely distributed in parts of Eurasia, Africa and South America (Deplazes et al., 2017).

pmc-12429798.title: Redefining Success in Hernia Surgery: The Case for Patient-Reported Outcomes
pmc-12429798.creator: Jacob Rosenberg, Anders Gram-Hanssen, Hugin Reistrup, Jason Joe Baker
pmc-12429798.description: In elective hernia surgery, the primary aim is to improve quality of life, rather than to save life. Therefore, outcome measures should emphasize domains such as pain, function, and overall satisfaction. While some principles also apply to other benign procedures, this perspective article centers on hernia repair as a paradigm for redefining surgical success.

pmc-12548077.title: Research progress on scar-free healing
pmc-12548077.creator: Wenhui Yang, Liu Liu, Xingjian Cheng
pmc-12548077.description: IntroductionPathological scars resulting from wound healing can cause functional impairment, cosmetic disfigurement, and psychological distress, highlighting the urgent need for regenerative solutions. Scar-free healing observed in embryonic development and some adult mammalian models have achieved complete tissue repair without fibrosis.MethodsThis article reviews literature on wound healing and scarless healing published over the past 25 years.

pmc-12625833.title: Risk stratification of IBD-associated liver disease using routinely collected biomarkers from a large-scale real-world dataset
pmc-12625833.creator: Zachary Green, Alex Z Kadhim, Lynn Win, Gabriela Czanner, Robert Mark Beattie, Sarah Ennis, James John Ashton
pmc-12625833.description: ObjectiveInflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-associated liver diseases (IBDALDs) are associated with hepatobiliary damage and malignancy, with diagnosis often delayed by heterogeneous presentation. We evaluated whether routinely collected biomarkers—at IBD diagnosis and during follow-up—can risk-stratify for IBDALD.MethodsThis observational retrospective longitudinal study included 1571 patients with IBD at University Hospital Southampton.

pmc-12675469.title: Development and validation of a nomogram for early prediction of macrolide-unresponsive Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children
pmc-12675469.creator: Hui Liu, Rina Sa, Yang Xin, Meilan Zhang, Hai Du
pmc-12675469.description: BackgroundMycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) is a leading cause of community-acquired pneumonia in children, with a significant increase in incidence following the COVID-19 pandemic. The emergence of macrolide-resistant M. pneumoniae (MRMP) has complicated treatment, leading to the concept of macrolide-unresponsive M. pneumoniae pneumonia (MUMPP), defined as lack of improvement after 72 h of macrolide therapy.

pmc-13165499.title: Contextual Predictability Modulates Neural Processing of Social Threat Words in High and Low Social Anxiety: Evidence from ERPs and Theta Oscillations
pmc-13165499.creator: Haichen Wang, Zhengjun Wang, Xiuxiu Zhang, Mutian Guo, Yaxi Duan, Qiusha Luo, Zhen Bi, Yue Du, Jianqin Cao
pmc-13165499.description: BackgroundIndividuals with high social anxiety (HSA) consistently exhibit attentional biases toward social threat. However, most evidence derives from paradigms in which threat and neutral stimuli are unpredictably intermixed, leaving it unclear whether such biases reflect heightened sensitivity to threat content per se or increased sensitivity to contextual unpredictability, where emotional valence changes unpredictably across trials.

pmc-13223045.title: Chronic anterior talofibular ligament rupture is associated with bilateral knee alterations and reduced ankle plantar flexor moment during gait
pmc-13223045.creator: Liufeng Xiao, Peiyao Liang, Lili Hu, Lin Guo, Lihang Zhang, Chengke Zhang, Molong Chen, Lisha Xu, Shikun Wen, Dianwei Li, Lin Ma
pmc-13223045.description: BackgroundWith the increasing clinical burden of ankle injuries, particularly anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) rupture, understanding their biomechanical impact on gait has gained renewed importance. While previous research has established local ankle deficits, the specific proximal compensatory mechanisms—particularly at the knee joint—in patients with MRI-confirmed complete ligamentous discontinuity remain insufficiently characterized.

pmc-13499626.title: HIV infection and survival in Hodgkin lymphoma: a real-world analysis of a multicenter research network
pmc-13499626.creator: Shih-Ping Lin, Tsung-Han Yen, Jian-Ri Li, Cheng-Wei Chou
pmc-13499626.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDespite effective antiretroviral therapy, people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) (PLWH) remain at a higher risk of developing Hodgkin lymphoma (HL). Further, survival disparities persist despite similar treatment recommendations.MethodsHerein, we present a global retrospective cohort study including data of adults (≥18 years) diagnosed with HL between 2015 and 2025 from the TriNetX database to evaluate the survival outcomes of Hodgkin lymphoma in HIV-infected vs non-HIV-infected patients and analyze the associated risk factors.
